title: Bandwidth-silo-aware prefill/decode pipeline and kernel fanout for mixed MIG H100/L40S/A10 fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: We will add a bandwidth-silo-aware layer to the prefill -> decode pipeline that dynamically paces prefill batches and selects kernel implementations based on per-MIG/sku memory bandwidth headroom and NVLink connectivity. Motivation: in mixed-sku heterogeneous clusters (H100/L40S/A10 with MIG partitions), memory and NVLink bandwidth contention during large concurrent prefill windows causes P95/P99 latency spikes and GPU DRAM saturation. Current kernel selection is primarily token-density and sequence-length driven; it does not incorporate live platform bandwidth signals. This task implements: 1) a lightweight per-MIG bandwidth headroom estimator surfaced to the runtime scheduler; 2) pacing gates for prefill windows that split large requests across time or NVLink islands to avoid DRAM bandwidth cliffs; 3) kernel fanout policy that prefers low-bandwidth kernels (e.g., quantized GEMM + attention tiling) when headroom is low, and higher-throughput tensor-core kernels when headroom is ample; 4) an experiment harness to validate across H100/L40S/A10 and mixed MIG partitions; 5) rollout and fallbacks to maintain SLA during behavioral regressions.
acceptance_criteria: P99 prefill tail latency reduced by >=20% on mixed workload synthetic replay compared to baseline (same request distribution)
End-to-end throughput (tokens/sec) degradation <=5% in steady-state on homogeneous H100 runs when feature is enabled
Automatic fallback to baseline kernel selection when telemetry is unavailable or inconsistent
Telemetry exposed in Console: per-MIG DRAM BW, NVLink util, kernel-choice counts, prefill pacing events
Canary rollout plan executed with no customer-facing incidents during 2-week canary
technical_approach: Add a sampling telemetry probe in the GPU agent that reports DRAM BW and NVLink utilization per-MIG every 250ms
Implement a lightweight estimator in the runtime scheduler that computes 'bandwidth headroom' = (DRAM BW capacity - observed BW) normalized by MIG size
Introduce prefill pacing policies: (a) temporal-slice: split large prefill across short windows, (b) island-affine: route parts of the prefill to different NVLink islands when topology allows
Extend kernel selector to accept headroom signal and score kernels by a composite metric (latency_cost / headroom_factor + bandwidth_cost), preferring quantized/tiling kernels under low headroom
Integrate clock-steer hints: when headroom consistently low, mark GPU candidate for short clock-up probes (subject to thermal policy) to evaluate net benefit
Create microbench harness with reproducible replay (1000 synthetic sessions) parameterized by seq_len, token_density, and concurrent_clients to validate across SKUs and MIG configs
experiment_plan: Phase 0: Microbench locally with single H100 (no MIG) to validate kernel scoring (2 days)
Phase 1: Controlled mixed-sku cluster internal canary (H100 + L40S + A10) with synthetic traffic; measure P50/P95/P99 and DRAM BW traces (3 days)
Phase 2: Canary on dedicated internal customer namespace on Dedicated fleet with 10% traffic routing and alerting (1 week)
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 100% for non-critical workloads while watching Console signals (2 weeks)
Rollback if p99 increases >10% or DRAM BW increases by >15% for more than 30 minutes
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Telemetry sampling adds overhead and noise -> Mitigation: 250ms sampling and aggregation; fall back to historical profiles if missing
Risk: Overly aggressive pacing reduces throughput -> Mitigation: enforce throughput floor and A/B test to tune pacing windows
Risk: Clock-steer probes could cause thermal nitration and oscillation -> Mitigation: integrate with thermal governor and limit probes per GPU per hour
Risk: Complexity of cross-NVLink routing may introduce bugs -> Mitigation: start with temporal-slicing only, enable island-affine in a second iteration after validation
implementation_tasks: Scheduler headroom estimator and API (owner: runtime-sched) - #2
Prefill pacing gates + policy configs (owner: runtime-sched) - #3
Kernel selector extension and scoring functions (owner: kernels) - #3
Console telemetry panels and alert rules (owner: console) - #1
Canary orchestration playbook and rollback hooks (owner: ops) - #1
